# Board game components and packaging manufacture — facts

> Source-anchored units about Board game components and packaging manufacture: 28 across 8 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## Structure and components

- [statement] Manufacturers offer packaging choices around the deck: LongPack lists telescope, tuck, tin, magnetic-lid and deck boxes; The Game Crafter distinguishes card-only tuck/hook boxes from larger boxes intended for games with parts. These are supplier-described capabilities. (medium confidence) — https://www.longpackgames.com/components/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture · also: https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/83-boxes
- [statement] LongPack's telescopic-box guideline calls for at least 15mm clearance in each dimension relative to the largest component, while also requiring capacity for all components together. Its example applies the allowance to folded boards, rules and punchboards. (low confidence) — https://help.longpackgames.com/article/58-telescopic-box · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] Panda requires a component specification sheet for designs that are not printed on paper. It supplies templates for printed boxes, game boards and cards. (low confidence) — https://pandagm.com/tools/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] Panda describes a pre-production copy covering printed box, rules, cards, punchboards and boards, accompanied by non-printed component samples. It then reviews a mass-production copy before assembling the remaining games. These are its described approval stages. (low confidence) — https://pandagm.com/our-process/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] PrintNinja warns that physical game proofs can include digitally printed components that are not color accurate, even though the proof arrives assembled. Approving an assembled proof therefore does not establish final color matching for those components. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/proofing-options/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] The Game Crafter says components that do not fit the selected game box can be packed outside that box in the shipping carton, potentially increasing shipping charges. A completed order therefore need not mean all components fit the retail box. (low confidence) (verified as of 2020-12-30) — https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/43-will-these-parts-fit-into-this-box · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] Panda offers folding boards and printed die-cut punchboards for tokens, tiles and other shapes; it warns that unique shapes and dual-layer mats require a die-cut mold and increase cost. (low confidence) — https://pandagm.com/components/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] Panda assigns a project manager from specification and pricing through production, reviews print files and component designs, then supplies a pre-production copy and nonprinted component samples for approval before mass production. (low confidence) — https://pandagm.com/our-process/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] Panda reviews a complete mass-production copy before final assembly and checks completeness as components enter the box; Scorpion Masqué also describes component QA and a full assembly check on production samples. (medium confidence) — https://pandagm.com/our-process/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture · also: https://www.scorpionmasque.com/en/blog/turing-machine-1st-printing-issues
- [statement] Under its no-box packing guidance, The Game Crafter uses plastic zippered baggies for smaller noncard components and brown paper banding for cards. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-05-22) — https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/623-how-will-my-game-components-be-packed-if-i-dont-include-a-box · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] Looney Labs explains that its folded, single-piece printed box parts use lighter material than wrapped setup boxes, feel more flexible and cost less to make; it also says hang-tab packaging supports some mass-market releases at lower production cost. These are its own packaging choices and economics. (low confidence) — https://faq.looneylabs.com/non-gameplay-questions/game-materials-faq · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In its January 2023 Turing Machine first-printing account, Scorpion Masqué acknowledged mostly missing or damaged inserts despite reviewing e-proofs, component samples and full assembly. This operator account documents a specific production failure. (low confidence) — https://www.hachetteboardgames.com/blogs/infos/turing-machine-1st-printing-issues · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Panda and LongPack advertise manufacturing of boxes, boards, wooden pieces and customized dice; these are manufacturer capability statements rather than independently measured quality or throughput. (medium confidence) — https://pandagm.com/components/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture · also: https://www.longpackgames.com/components/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] LongPack advertises folding game boards with reinforced edges, different papers and finishes, and die-cut double-board options. This is a supplier capability statement. (low confidence) — https://www.longpackgames.com/components/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] LongPack lists stock wooden meeples, cubes, discs and triangles plus custom wooden shapes; it describes painting and laser engraving as decoration options. (low confidence) — https://www.longpackgames.com/components/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] LongPack describes dice made from wood, resin or acrylic, customized through engraving, laser cutting or printing. This is a manufacturing capability statement. (low confidence) — https://www.longpackgames.com/components/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] LongPack specifies 20mm of artwork bleed per side for telescopic-box top and bottom files: 3mm standard bleed plus 17mm wrap margin. This is its box-specific requirement. (low confidence) — https://help.longpackgames.com/article/58-telescopic-box · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] PrintNinja offers shaped vacuum-formed plastic organizers and printable cardstock dividers for two-piece boxes; its stated cardstock compartment shapes are squares or rectangles. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/custom-board-game-organizers/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] LongPack's punchboard guide specifies approximately 8mm x 8mm as its smallest token size, a minimum 3mm edge on custom shapes, and at least 6mm between dielines. These are supplier-specific design limits. (low confidence) — https://help.longpackgames.com/article/63-punchboard · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] LongPack instructs designers to separate punchboard dielines from regular artwork and mirror the back-side layout. It also recommends identifying similar diecut molds with marks or numbers to prevent mixing. (low confidence) — https://help.longpackgames.com/article/63-punchboard · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] LongPack says each punchboard diecut mold adds cost and suggests reusing one dieline template across multiple punchboards where the layout permits. (low confidence) — https://help.longpackgames.com/article/63-punchboard · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] PrintNinja's game-proof options include instruction sheets, accordion instructions, saddle-stitched booklets and perfect-bound booklets; its listed instruction proofs use digital printing. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/proofing-options/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] Panda offers a one-piece tuckbox for a game consisting of cards and a paper sheet, as well as internal tuckboxes for larger games; LongPack lists telescope, tuck, magnetic-lid, tin and deck boxes. (medium confidence) — https://pandagm.com/components/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture · also: https://www.longpackgames.com/components/
- [statement] Panda describes cardboard trays as internal organizers and protection during shipping, and vacuum-formed plastic trays as organizers for play and storage. (low confidence) — https://pandagm.com/components/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] Panda offers printed, folded paper sheets for rules and player aids; it describes saddle-stitched rulebooks with page counts in groups of four and recommends other bindings for longer books. (low confidence) — https://pandagm.com/components/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] LongPack lists stock wooden meeples, cubes and discs alongside custom shapes, with paint or laser engraving; it lists wood, resin and acrylic dice customized by engraving, laser cutting or printing. (low confidence) — https://www.longpackgames.com/components/ · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] LongPack attributes possible punchboard front/back misalignment during short pre-production periods to moisture-driven paper expansion, says linen texture can worsen it, and describes dehumidification during mass production; it also identifies layering and rough edges as sample risks. (low confidence) — https://help.longpackgames.com/article/111-14-punch-board-player-board · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture
- [statement] In its January 2023 first-printing notice, Scorpion Masqué reported missing or damaged Turing Machine inserts despite describing electronic-proof and assembly checks; it said future-printing files had been reviewed with the factory. This documents a specific publisher incident, not an industry defect rate. (low confidence) — https://www.scorpionmasque.com/en/blog/turing-machine-1st-printing-issues · keywords: Board game components and packaging manufacture · also: https://www.hachetteboardgames.com/blogs/infos/turing-machine-1st-printing-issues
